name: The Nature of the Church (Visible and Invisible)
path: Ecclesiology: The Doctrine of the Church

objectives.text: Identify the church as God's people rather than a building
Name believers together as the family of God who belong to one household
Recall from Jesus' words to Peter that Jesus builds His church and keeps it safe
Describe what the first Christians did together when they gathered as the church
Explain how Paul's picture of the body shows that every member of the church belongs and is needed
Identify Christ as the only head of the church using passages from Paul's letters
Explain the difference between the invisible church of all the elect and the visible church of all who profess the true faith
Compare a local congregation with the universal or catholic church spread through all times and places
Explain why the Reformed tradition teaches that the visible church includes the children of believers
Describe biblical ways members of a local church are called to serve and build one another up
Analyze what the biblical images of the church as body, bride, temple, and flock each teach about its nature
Explain from Jesus' parables why the visible church on earth contains both true believers and those who only profess faith
Trace the continuity of the one people of God from Israel to the New Testament church
Explain how the unity of the church rests on the union of its members with Christ their head
Explain the Reformed teaching on the communion of the saints including the shared gifts and mutual duties of believers
Analyze how the visible and invisible distinction guards against both equating church membership with salvation and dismissing the visible church
Explain the confessional teaching that outside the visible church there is no ordinary possibility of salvation and the duty to join it
Compare the Reformed doctrine of the nature of the church with Roman Catholic and broadly individualistic evangelical views
Evaluate the claim that a Christian can live faithfully apart from the church using Scripture and the confessions
Explain from Scripture and the Heidelberg Catechism how Christ gathers, defends, and preserves His church throughout history
Compose a structured essay presenting a biblical and confessional doctrine of the church as visible and invisible, local and catholic

changes: Kept and reworded the real competencies (people not building, family of God, Jesus builds His church, body of Christ, visible and invisible, local and catholic, biblical images, covenant people, union with Christ, communion of saints, individualism, gathering and preserving). Replaced the vague observe objective with a text-based Acts 2 description, and recast the apply call to belong and love as describing biblical duties of members so it no longer targets feelings. Merged the construct and defend items into one evaluation objective and one capstone composition. Added missing competencies: Christ as sole head, children of believers in the visible church, the mixed visible church from the parables, the distinction's role against opposite errors, no ordinary salvation outside the visible church, and comparison with other traditions' views. Narrowed scripture to verse ranges and added precise confessional anchors (WCF 25.1, 25.2, 25.5, 25.6, 26.1, 26.2, 7.6, WLC Q62, Q64, Q66, HC Q54, Q55, Belgic 27, 28). Left marks, government, sacraments, worship, and mission to sibling sub-topics.
